title: Shabana Azmi, Naseeruddin Shah Join Mumbai Protest Demanding Election Chief's Ouster
excerpt: Thousands gathered at Shivaji Park for the Cockroach Janta Party's demonstration seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral-roll irregularities.
body:
• Thousands gathered at Mumbai's Shivaji Park on Friday for a protest organized by the Cockroach Janta Party demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
  • Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi and composer-singer Vishal Dadlani joined the demonstration, alongside student groups including the SFI and AISF.
  • The protest centers on alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, after reports that two election commissioners objected to decisions taken without their knowledge.
  • Mumbai Police had denied permission for the gathering; the CJP responded by launching a "Jail Bharo Andolan," daring authorities to arrest the protesters.

Mumbai's Shivaji Park turned into a sea of protesters on Friday, October 2, as thousands gathered for a demonstration organized by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi and composer-singer Vishal Dadlani joined the protest, lending star power to an agitation that went ahead despite Mumbai Police denying permission for the gathering.

Star power at Shivaji Park

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke shared video footage of an interaction with Naseeruddin Shah, in which the veteran actor expressed his gratitude to the organizer. An emotional Dipke described the moment as a significant honor, noting his surprise at Shah's attendance. According to Zoom TV, footage circulating on social media showed the celebrities interacting with attendees and organizers at the venue.

Shabana Azmi, who has previously joined public demonstrations on issues such as the NEET examination controversy, addressed the gathering. She emphasized the importance of the right to protest, particularly when citizens have concerns about the removal of names from electoral rolls. Vishal Dadlani, who had announced his participation in the October 2 demonstration in advance through a video, raised the slogan "Go Gyanu Go" and urged the crowd to join in, questioning what people would do if they lost the power to vote, linking his remarks to the controversy over electoral-roll revisions.

"Protest is our right, and people must protest when their names are removed from the electoral rolls."

— Shabana Azmi, addressing the Shivaji Park gathering

According to InShorts, composer Vishal Bhardwaj and singer Rekha Bhardwaj also joined the demonstration, while actor Prakash Raj expressed support. Student organizations including the Students' Federation of India (SFI) and the All India Students' Federation (AISF) participated, with AISF groups from Pune bringing musical instruments and leading slogans near the perimeter of the park.

What the protest is about

The CJP's agitation targets alleged irregularities in the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protest follows media reports that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on multiple occasions over a ten-month period regarding decisions linked to the revision, with some decisions and orders allegedly issued without their full knowledge, according to reports cited by Zoom TV and Andhra Vilas. At least 14 such occasions were reported.

In response to those reports, the Election Commission of India issued a clarification stating that all decisions, including those pertaining to the SIR, were reached unanimously by the three-member commission. The flashpoint for protesters remains the deletion of names from electoral rolls, an issue Azmi raised directly in her address to the gathering.

Denied permission, then "Jail Bharo"

Mumbai Police had earlier denied permission for the planned gathering. The CJP responded by announcing a "Jail Bharo Andolan" — a fill-the-jails agitation — with protesters marching from Shiv Sena Bhavan toward Shivaji Park carrying the Tricolour and party flags, raising slogans calling for Kumar's resignation. Dipke publicly challenged Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to arrest the protesters and send them to jail, and warned of escalating the stir if the CEC does not resign.

The demonstration also drew a counter-protest. A group identifying itself as "Gen Next Mumbai" gathered beneath the statue of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, accusing Dipke of speaking about dismantling the Constitution and staging what they called a peaceful demonstration to uphold and respect it.

The diaspora angle

Electoral integrity debates in India are watched closely by the diaspora. NRIs with family members voting back home follow controversies over voter rolls with personal interest, and the perceived health of Indian democracy is a recurring subject in overseas Indian discourse. When film personalities of the stature of Shah and Azmi take a public stand on the functioning of the Election Commission, the story travels well beyond Shivaji Park.

What to watch

The immediate questions are whether the Election Commission responds to the resignation demand, whether Mumbai Police take action over the unauthorized gathering, and how far the CJP takes its threatened escalation. With the SIR controversy already producing an official clarification from the Commission, the protest adds street-level pressure to an institutional dispute that shows no sign of settling.
image_caption: Protesters gather at Shivaji Park in Mumbai during the Cockroach Janta Party demonstration on October 2. Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi and singer Vishal Dadlani joined the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
nri_angle: The protest over electoral-roll integrity resonates with NRIs who closely follow the health of Indian democracy and have family members voting back home.
